title: Discrepancy in Southwest Georgia Flips Key State House Seat to GOP
snippet: A discovery of nearly 400 uncounted votes in Seminole County has put Republican incumbent Gerald Greene ahead, narrowing the Democrats' margin in the Georgia House.
content:
ATLANTA — A high-stakes Georgia state House election has taken a dramatic turn after election officials discovered 388 previously unrecorded votes in rural southwest Georgia, flipping a key contest in favor of the Republican incumbent.

The vote revision in House District 154 has shifted the lead from Democratic challenger Harry James to longtime Republican incumbent Gerald Greene. Prior to the discovery during routine checks in Seminole County, James held a narrow 58-vote margin over Greene. Following the inclusion of the newly tallied ballots, Greene now holds a 262-vote lead.

State Officials Launch Investigation

Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger announced a formal probe into the incident to determine why nearly 400 ballots were omitted from initial election night figures and whether proper election protocols were breached.

"This oversight didn’t just affect the numbers — it changed who was leading an election," Raffensperger said in a statement. "That is unacceptable, and we intend to find out exactly how it happened."

The discrepancy came to light when state election monitors noticed that voter check-in logs at Seminole County polling locations exceeded the number of cast ballots reported. While early reports suggested a missing memory card, Seminole County Elections Supervisor Ron Foskey clarified that all digital media cards were accounted for on election night. Foskey attributed the error to an incomplete final validation step in the election management software, confirming that updated totals matched internal scanner records.

High Stakes for Legislative Power

The updated totals carry heavy political weight in Atlanta. Democrats were initially on track to capture control of the Georgia House of Representatives for the first time in over two decades. With District 154 leaning back toward Republicans, the Democratic majority drops to 92 seats in the 180-member chamber—just one seat above the 91 needed to hold control.

The balance of power remains further unsettled by another unresolved race in House District 138, where Republican state Rep. Mike Cheokas faces Democrat Ethan Wolfe in a Dec. 1 runoff election.

District 154 is also notable due to its demographic makeup. Greene, who originally took office as a Democrat in 1982 before switching to the GOP following the 2010 cycle, is currently the only Republican in the Georgia General Assembly representing a majority-Black district.

With county election boards facing a Monday deadline to officially certify their election results, state investigators are continuing to audit Seminole County’s procedures to ensure accurate reporting in future cycles.
